current_activity: XII Corps attacks from the Odon bridgehead to secure the Bougy-Evrecy road before Goodwood
notes: Event date: 15 July 1944, night (Ellis, vol. I, p. 334). Event definition: On the night of 15 July the preliminary attacks begin across the front between the west of Caen and Tilly-sur-Seulles; XII Corps, starting from the Odon bridgehead, is to secure a firm base on the road south-east from Bougy through Evrecy with a view to an advance towards Aunay-sur-Odon or Thury-Harcourt; it fights hard and continuously until Goodwood begins on 18 July (p. 334). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 334: "Preliminary British operations began on the night of the 15th with attacks which extended across the whole front between the west of Caen and Tilly"; "XII Corps starting from the Odon bridgehead was first to secure a firm base on the road running south- east from Bougy through Evrecy". Location: Odon bridgehead (existing place PL0256) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the Odon bridgehead from which the corps started; the corps headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names the Odon bridgehead as the start and the Bougy-Evrecy road as the objective; no corps headquarters place is given.
